name: MA-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Stephen Lynch running with large financial advantage
Republican Burke raised only ~$1,500 and has negative cash on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~98%
model.rationale: Lynch is a long-serving incumbent in a D+15 district with a $640K cash advantage over a Republican who raised essentially nothing, and markets price his win at 98%. No polls or ratings contradict the fundamentals, so the safe-D assessment stands.
model.watch: A surprise outside-spending surge for Burke or an unexpected Lynch scandal could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Stephen Lynch, a Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Massachusetts district that leans Democratic by about fifteen points. He holds a large financial edge, with roughly $640,000 on hand, while Republican Robert Burke has raised about $1,500 and reports negative cash on hand. Outside groups have spent modestly against Lynch, but nothing suggests a competitive race.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets give Lynch about a 98% chance of winning. The forecast is a Safe Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
